summary:
Artificial intelligence continues reshaping healthcare operations across multiple fronts. Assort Health secured $120 million to expand its patient journey AI agents, while Mount Sinai is enlisting Signal 1 to manage its expanding AI portfolio—underscoring how health systems are betting heavily on AI but recognizing they need better governance structures. Healthcare IT leaders are being cautioned to strengthen foundational systems before scaling AI initiatives, particularly as AI applications address cognitive burden in clinical settings and accelerate revenue cycle processes.

Beyond AI infrastructure, the sector is tackling broader healthcare delivery challenges. The CDC is advancing its public health data strategy to modernize disease tracking and response, while patient education gaps in breast cancer care highlight persistent gaps in how information reaches patients. On the pharmaceutical front, the FDA's new approval for Gilead's breast cancer drug maintains competitive pressure in an active treatment landscape.
